questions.question:
Select the option that best defines the given word.

Jovial
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Friendly and in good mood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Jovial"** refers to someone who is cheerful, friendly, and in a good mood. (मिलनसार और अच्छे मूड में)
 
 
• **Example:** Despite the challenges, he remained jovial and spread positivity wherever he went.
 
 
• Hence, the word "Jovial" accurately reflects the definition of being friendly and in good spirits.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Friendly and in good mood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: Very cautious** (बहुत सतर्क): Refers to someone who is extremely careful or alert about possible dangers or problems.
 
 
• **Example:** She was very cautious while walking on the icy road.
 
 

 
• **Option 3: Angry** (गुस्सैल): Refers to someone feeling strong displeasure or hostility.
 
 
• **Example:** He was angry at being ignored during the meeting.
 
 

 
• **Option 4: Pensive mood** (चिंतनशील मूड): Refers to a state of being deeply thoughtful, often in a melancholic way.
 
 
• **Example:** She sat by the window, lost in a pensive mood, thinking about her future.

questions.question: Select the sentence that contains the meaning of the word 'incorrigible'.

options.text: Modern technology has enabled paints to last longer and retain their freshness.
He is a very bad liar beyond correction.
The weather is very warm with no sign of abating.
The teacher found the mid-day meal too salty to eat.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"incorrigible"** refers to someone or something that is incapable of being corrected, improved, or reformed. (असुधारनीय)

 
 
• **Example:** Despite numerous warnings, his incorrigible habit of procrastination remained unchanged.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "He is a very bad liar beyond correction" aligns with the meaning of "incorrigible," as it suggests that the person cannot be corrected or changed. (असुधारनीय)
 
 
• **Example:** The student was incorrigible, constantly disrupting the class despite repeated attempts to discipline him.
 
 
 
• Hence, Option 2 correctly captures the essence of the word "incorrigible."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1:** "Modern technology has enabled paints to last longer and retain their freshness." This refers to durability and freshness, not to the inability to be corrected. (टिकाऊपन और ताजगी)

 
 
• **Example:** The newly developed paint is designed to last for years without fading.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "The weather is very warm with no sign of abating." This describes persistent weather conditions, but it does not relate to being beyond correction. (मौसम की गर्मी)
 
 
• **Example:** The summer heat persisted throughout the month with no sign of relief.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "The teacher found the mid-day meal too salty to eat." This describes the taste of the food, which does not match the meaning of "incorrigible." (बहुत ज्यादा नमकीन)
 
 
• **Example:** The soup was too salty to enjoy, so I decided to skip it.

questions.question: All of the following options, except one, contain sentences in the Future tense. Select the grammatically INCORRECT sentence.

options.text: I am sure you will pass the exam.
The jacket will look nice on you.
I think we will meeting again before long.
I think you will like George if you meet him.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Option 3 contains a grammatical error in the sentence: **"I think we will meeting again before long."**
 
• The verb form "**meeting**" is incorrect in this context as it is not in the future tense.
 
• In future tense sentences, the structure should be "will + base verb" (e.g., "will meet").
 
• The correct sentence should be: **"I think we will meet again before long."**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I think we will meet again before long."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "I am sure you will pass the exam."** – This sentence is grammatically correct and in future tense.
 
• **Option 2: "The jacket will look nice on you."** – This sentence is grammatically correct and in future tense.
 
• **Option 4: "I think you will like George if you meet him."** – This sentence is grammatically correct and in future tense.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Determine the collocation through the sentence.

He suffers from __________ pain in the joints.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**excruciating**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**excruciating**" means intensely painful.
 
• It collocates perfectly with the word "pain" to describe severe discomfort.
 
• Other options like "**quick**," "**awkward**," and "**external**" do not fit the context appropriately.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *He suffers from excruciating__ pain in the joints.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Quick**: refers to something happening with speed, which does not fit the context.
 
• **Awkward**: means causing discomfort or embarrassment, which is unrelated to pain.
 
• **External**: means outside or outer, which does not describe the nature of the pain.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

He __has been writing most articles__ and has given presentations on his research.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence states that someone has been writing articles and giving presentations on their research.
 
• The phrase "has been writing" implies an ongoing action, but "most articles" is incorrect and sounds vague.
 
• The substitution "has written several articles" makes the sentence grammatically correct and precise.
 
• It correctly conveys the idea of completed actions in the present perfect tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He has written several articles and has given presentations on his research."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "was write many articles" – This is grammatically incorrect as it uses the wrong verb tense and structure.
 
• **Option 3:** "had written few articles" – This is incorrect as it uses the past perfect tense, which is not suitable for the given context.
 
• **Option 4: **"will write more articles" – This is incorrect as it refers to future actions, which is not relevant to the sentence.

questions.question:

questions.question: Identify the sentence with the INCORRECT usage of an adverb.

options.text: He usually goes for a run in the morning.
He often goes for a run in the morning.
He goes always for a run in the morning.
He always goes for a run in the morning.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence **"He goes always for a run in the morning"** has an incorrect placement of the adverb "always."
 
• Adverbs like "always" are generally placed before the main verb or after auxiliary verbs.
 
• The correct sentence should be **"He always goes for a run in the morning."**
 
• Thus, the error is in the word order of Option 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He always goes for a run in the morning."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "He usually goes for a run in the morning" – This sentence is grammatically correct and uses the adverb "usually" appropriately.
 
• **Option 2:** "He often goes for a run in the morning" – This sentence is grammatically correct and uses the adverb "often" correctly.
 
• **Option 4:** "He always goes for a run in the morning" – This sentence is grammatically correct and uses the adverb "always" in the proper position.
